title: Introspective calibration and schema checks for tokenized function outputs under FP8/INT8
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Under low-precision deployments (FP8/INT8) we see intermittent schema nonconformance in function-call outputs even when token-level logprobs look reasonable. Failures are often subtle (truncated JSON, split tokens in keys, unexpected extra commas) and surface only on long or adversarial examples.

Goal: Build an "introspective" calibration + validation workflow that pairs profile-aware quantization calibration with token-aware schema enforcement checks so we can detect, categorize, and mitigate structured-output regressions introduced by quantization. Success is defined as: schema-conformance failure rate <= 0.2% on our validation corpus for INT8/FP8 quantized variants, and clear mitigations (prompt-level or runtime canonicalizers) with <5% throughput/cost overhead.

Proposed approach summary:
1) Augmented calibration corpus: augment the existing calibration dataset with token-boundary stress cases (long keys, unicode separators, nested arrays, escaped quotes) and adversarially generated examples that target tokenizer splits and KV cache boundary conditions.
2) Tokenized introspection layer: at calibration time collect token-level activation statistics (per-layer, per-head) aligned to token boundaries for samples that produce function-call structured outputs. This lets us compute calibration scales conditioned on token types (delimiters, JSON punctuation, identifier tokens).
3) Schema-aware fuzz harness: implement a test harness that replays prompts through quantized runtimes and asserts JSON schema conformance, but also classifies failures (truncation, invalid punctuation, wrong types, extraneous keys). The harness will include controlled truncation, token-split injection, and KV-cache warm/cold scenarios.
4) Mitigations: evaluate a spectrum of fixes from non-invasive to heavy: soft delimiters in prompt engineering, post-output canonicalizers that repair token-split-induced corruption, and narrow per-op quantization overrides for attention/query/key/value kernels when schema failures spike.
5) CI gating and dashboards: add schema-failure metrics to the Console per-model/profile and gate quantization pushes via a quality score computed over the harness.

Tradeoffs and considerations:
- Per-token conditioned calibration increases calibration time and metadata size; trade throughput at calibration time vs runtime correctness.
- Per-op quantization overrides can reduce unit cost advantages of full INT8/FP8 but may be necessary for high-SLA models.
- Prompt-level mitigations are cheap but brittle; canonicalizers add latency and must be evaluated for failure modes (incorrect repairs).

Acceptance criteria:
- New calibration corpus committed + review doc in Confluence (link in attachments).
- Test harness added to e2e-quant-tests with deterministic seed and baseline pass rate recorded.
- INT8 and FP8 profile candidates show <=0.2% schema-conformance failures on held-out validation suite.
- Runbook for mitigations and rollout plan for runtime-1.22 documented and approved by Runtime and QA leads.
comments: 2026-01-20 - Spike completed: tokenizer split hypothesis validated on a 3k sample; function names with underscores and long keys trigger split tokens that break JSON reconstruction. Next: expand calibration samples to include these patterns. -- Marco

2026-01-29 - Design review: agreed to collect token-aligned activation stats during calibration. Decision: store summary histograms (per-layer Q/D range) not raw tensors to limit storage. Action: ENG infra to add histogram output to calibration pipeline. -- Aisha

2026-02-12 - Early harness run: INT8 candidate A produced 0.85% schema failures on validation set, FP8 candidate B at 0.28%. Failures clustered on nested arrays + escaped unicode. Pinned failing cases in /drive and added to corpus. -- Marco

2026-02-20 - Perf tradeoff analysis: per-op override for attention kernels increases p50 token latency by ~3.5% but reduces failures to 0.12% in canary. Need product decision on acceptable latency vs correctness. -- Performance team (review)
2026-02-28 - PR feedback (runtime#4821): request to add deterministic seed handling for fuzzing and CI gating hook. Also small comment to normalize whitespace in canonicalizer. -- PR reviewer: S. Kim

2026-03-05 - QA run: added KV-cache warm/cold scenarios; observed an additional class of truncation when cache becomes stale after rollbacks. Follow-up: add cache-consistency check to replay harness. -- QA

2026-03-10 - Next steps: finalize calibration corpus, land per-token histogram output, extend e2e-quant-tests to classify failures and emit dashboard metrics. Schedule canary rollout to 5% of dedicated capacity for runtime-1.22. -- Marco
